cohort: The study cohort consisted of 556 newborns (median age 5 days, range 0-5 days) diagnosed with clavicle fractures, humerus fractures, or brachial plexus injuries secondary to birth trauma.
finding: Larger head circumference was associated with an increased risk of clavicle fractures and brachial plexus injuries (BPI), while higher birth weight and lower 1-minute APGAR scores were also linked to increased BPI incidence.
